name: Mathematics
description: Mathematics from arithmetic and algebra through calculus, proof and the major pure branches (algebra, analysis, geometry, topology, number theory, combinatorics) to probability, statistics, numerical and applied mathematics, organised along the MSC2020 classification.

chapters.name: Arithmetic & Pre-Algebra
chapters.summary: Whole numbers, fractions, decimals, percentages, ratios, negative numbers and first use of variables: the bedrock every later chapter assumes.

topics.name: Place value, whole numbers and the four operations
Order of operations and mental arithmetic
Factors, multiples, primes, GCD and LCM
Percentages, percentage change and simple interest
Negative numbers and the number line
Exponents, square roots and scientific notation
Variables, expressions and simple one-step equations

chapters.name: Elementary & Intermediate Algebra
chapters.summary: Manipulating expressions and solving equations, inequalities, polynomials and systems, which is the working language of all later mathematics.

topics.name: Algebraic expressions, like terms and the distributive law
Linear equations and inequalities in one variable
Graphing lines: slope, intercepts and forms of a linear equation
Quadratic equations: factoring, completing the square and the quadratic formula
Radical equations and absolute-value equations and inequalities
Word problems and translating situations into equations

chapters.name: Euclidean Geometry
chapters.summary: Classical plane and solid geometry, from angles and triangles to congruence, similarity, circles, area and volume, and a first taste of proof.

topics.name: Points, lines, planes and angles; parallel lines and transversals
Triangles: congruence criteria and angle sums
Circles: chords, tangents, arcs and inscribed angles
Transformations: translations, rotations, reflections and dilations
Euclid's axioms and writing geometric proofs

chapters.name: Trigonometry
chapters.summary: Angles, the trigonometric functions, identities and triangle solving, needed for waves, rotations, vectors and calculus.

topics.name: Angles in degrees and radians; arc length and sector area
Right-triangle trigonometry: sine, cosine and tangent
The unit circle and trigonometric functions of any angle
Graphs of sine, cosine and tangent: amplitude, period and phase shift
Sum, difference, double-angle and half-angle formulas
Law of sines and law of cosines; area of a triangle
Applications: bearings, heights, distances and periodic models

chapters.name: Precalculus
chapters.summary: Functions and their graphs, polynomial, rational, exponential and logarithmic functions, complex numbers and basic vectors: the direct preparation for calculus.

topics.name: Functions: domain, range, notation and graphs
Transformations and combinations of functions; composition
Linear and quadratic functions and models
Polynomial functions: zeros, factor theorem and end behaviour
Exponential functions and growth and decay models
Logarithms: properties, change of base and solving equations
Complex numbers: arithmetic, polar form and De Moivre's theorem
Vectors in the plane: components, dot product and applications
Systems of equations and an introduction to matrices
Sequences, series and the binomial theorem
Intuitive idea of a limit and rates of change

chapters.name: Analytic Geometry
chapters.summary: Geometry done with coordinates: lines, conic sections, polar coordinates and parametric curves in the plane and in space.

topics.name: Distance, midpoint and equations of lines and circles

sub.name: Rotation of axes and the general conic

topics.name: Vectors in two and three dimensions
Lines, planes and quadric surfaces in three dimensions
Coordinate transformations: translation and rotation of axes

chapters.name: Calculus
chapters.summary: Single-variable calculus from limits and derivatives to integrals, integration techniques and applications: the central tool of science and engineering.

topics.name: Limits: intuitive idea, limit laws and one-sided limits
Continuity and the intermediate value theorem
Formal epsilon-delta definition of a limit

sub.name: Derivative as slope and rate of change
Power, product, quotient and chain rules
Derivatives of trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions

topics.name: Mean value theorem and curve sketching

sub.name: Riemann sums and the definite integral

topics.name: Integration techniques: integration by parts, trigonometric integrals and substitution
Applications of integration: area, volume, arc length and surface area
Physical applications: work, fluid force, centre of mass
Separable differential equations and exponential growth models
Calculus with parametric curves and polar coordinates

chapters.name: Sequences & Series
chapters.summary: Convergence of sequences and infinite series, convergence tests, power series and Taylor series, which underpin approximation and analysis.

topics.name: Sequences: limits, monotone and bounded sequences
Infinite series and partial sums; geometric and telescoping series
Divergence test and the integral test; p-series
Alternating series and absolute versus conditional convergence
Ratio and root tests; choosing a test
Power series: radius and interval of convergence
Taylor and Maclaurin series of standard functions
Taylor's theorem and error bounds for approximations
Applications: approximating functions, limits and integrals
Introduction to Fourier series as another kind of expansion

chapters.name: Multivariable Calculus
chapters.summary: Calculus of functions of several variables: partial derivatives, gradients, optimisation with constraints and multiple integrals.

topics.name: Vectors and the geometry of space: dot and cross products, lines and planes
Vector-valued functions, space curves, arc length and curvature
Functions of several variables (multivariable calculus): graphs, level sets, limits and continuity
Differentiability, linearisation and the multivariable chain rule
Local extrema, the second-derivative test and optimisation
Double integrals over general regions; polar coordinates
Triple integrals in cylindrical and spherical coordinates
Change of variables and the Jacobian
Applications: mass, centre of mass, moments and probability

chapters.name: Vector Calculus
chapters.summary: Vector fields, line and surface integrals, divergence and curl, and the theorems of Green, Stokes and Gauss that underpin physics and engineering.

topics.name: Vector fields (vector calculus): conservative fields and potential functions
Line integrals of scalar functions and vector fields; work
Fundamental theorem for line integrals and path independence
Divergence and curl: meaning and identities
Curvilinear coordinates: grad, div, curl and Laplacian in cylindrical and spherical coordinates
Applications to fluid flow, electromagnetism and conservation laws
Preview of differential forms and the generalised Stokes theorem

chapters.name: Introduction to Proofs & Mathematical Reasoning
chapters.summary: How to read and write mathematical proofs: logic, quantifiers, sets, functions, induction and proof techniques, the gateway to pure mathematics.

topics.name: Propositional logic: connectives, truth tables and implication
Direct proof and proof by contrapositive
Functions: injective, surjective, bijective and inverses
Cardinality: finite, countable and uncountable sets
Divisibility and modular arithmetic as a proving ground
Reading, writing and critiquing proofs; counterexamples

chapters.name: Set Theory
chapters.summary: Sets, relations, cardinals and ordinals, from naive set theory to the ZFC axioms that serve as the standard foundation of mathematics.

topics.name: The axiom of choice, Zorn's lemma and the well-ordering theorem
The continuum hypothesis and independence results (forcing overview)

chapters.name: Logic & Proof Theory
chapters.summary: Mathematical logic: propositional and first-order logic, formal proof systems, completeness and the incompleteness theorems.

topics.name: Propositional logic: syntax, semantics and completeness
First-order logic: languages, structures and satisfaction
Peano arithmetic and Goedel's incompleteness theorems

chapters.name: Model Theory
chapters.summary: Studies mathematical structures through the first-order sentences they satisfy, linking logic with algebra and geometry.

topics.name: Quantifier elimination (dense linear orders, algebraically closed and real closed fields)

chapters.name: Recursion & Computability
chapters.summary: Recursion theory proper: degrees of unsolvability, the arithmetical hierarchy and the fine structure of what can and cannot be computed.

topics.name: Many-one and Turing reducibility; Turing degrees

chapters.name: Category Theory
chapters.summary: The language of objects and structure-preserving maps (functors, natural transformations, limits, adjunctions) that unifies algebra, topology and logic.

topics.name: Universal properties and the Yoneda lemma

chapters.name: Discrete Mathematics
chapters.summary: First course in discrete mathematics: logic, sets, counting, relations, recurrences, graphs and trees, essential for computer science and proof-based maths.

topics.name: Counting: product and sum rules, permutations and combinations
Recurrence relations and solving linear recurrences
Elementary number theory: divisibility, primes and modular arithmetic
Graphs: paths, connectivity, Euler and Hamilton circuits
Asymptotic notation and growth of functions

chapters.name: Graph Theory
chapters.summary: Graphs and networks: connectivity, trees, matchings, colouring, planarity and flows, with applications across computing and science.

topics.name: Paths, cycles, connectivity and Menger's theorem

chapters.name: Enumerative Combinatorics
chapters.summary: Systematic counting: permutations, inclusion-exclusion, recurrences, generating functions and partitions.

topics.name: Counting under symmetry: Burnside's lemma and Polya enumeration

chapters.name: Combinatorial Designs
chapters.summary: Balanced arrangements such as block designs, Latin squares and Steiner systems, used in experimental design and coding.

chapters.name: Ramsey Theory
chapters.summary: Why complete disorder is impossible: Ramsey numbers and the theorems of Ramsey, van der Waerden and Hales-Jewett.

topics.name: Pigeonhole principle and Ramsey's theorem for graphs

chapters.name: Probabilistic Combinatorics
chapters.summary: The probabilistic method and random discrete structures, proving existence by showing a random object works.

chapters.name: Algebraic Combinatorics
chapters.summary: Combinatorics meets algebra: symmetric functions, Young tableaux, posets and their links to representation theory.

chapters.name: Extremal Combinatorics
chapters.summary: How large or small a structure can be while avoiding a pattern: Turan-type problems, Sperner families and intersecting families.

chapters.name: Matroid Theory
chapters.summary: Matroids abstract the idea of independence from linear algebra and graphs, and explain when greedy algorithms work.

chapters.name: Coding Theory (Combinatorial Aspects)
chapters.summary: Combinatorial bounds and constructions for codes, including block codes and network coding.

topics.name: Bounds on codes: Hamming, Singleton, Plotkin and Gilbert-Varshamov

chapters.name: Linear Algebra
chapters.summary: Vectors, matrices, linear maps, determinants, eigenvalues and orthogonality: the most widely used branch of mathematics after calculus.

topics.name: Systems of linear equations and Gaussian elimination

sub.name: Matrix of a linear map and change of basis

topics.name: Diagonalisation and the spectral theorem for symmetric matrices
Quadratic forms and positive definite matrices
Applications: Markov chains, differential equations and computer graphics

chapters.name: Abstract Algebra
chapters.summary: Groups, rings and fields: the axiomatic study of algebraic structure that underlies number theory, geometry and cryptography.

topics.name: Binary operations and the definition of a group; examples
Cyclic groups, Lagrange's theorem and cosets
Homomorphisms, normal subgroups, quotients and isomorphism theorems

chapters.name: Group Theory
chapters.summary: Deeper group theory: group actions, Sylow theorems, solvable and simple groups, permutation groups and presentations.

topics.name: Solvable, nilpotent and simple groups; composition series

chapters.name: Ring Theory
chapters.summary: Rings, ideals and factorisation: integral domains, PIDs, UFDs, polynomial rings and an introduction to noncommutative rings and modules.

topics.name: Ideals, quotient rings and the isomorphism theorems
Modules over a PID and the structure theorem
Semisimple rings and the Artin-Wedderburn theorem

chapters.name: Field Theory
chapters.summary: Field extensions and Galois theory, explaining which polynomial equations are solvable by radicals and which constructions are possible.

chapters.name: Representation Theory

topics.name: Tensor products, induced and restricted representations; Frobenius reciprocity
Burnside's pq theorem and other applications
Introduction to representations of compact groups (SU(2), SO(3))

chapters.name: Matrix Analysis & Multilinear Algebra
chapters.summary: Advanced matrix theory and multilinear algebra: canonical forms, norms, positive definite matrices, perturbation of eigenvalues and tensor products.

topics.name: Similarity, Jordan canonical form and the rational canonical form
Unitary similarity, Schur triangularisation and normal matrices
Hermitian and positive definite matrices; Cholesky and square roots
Variational characterisation of eigenvalues (Courant-Fischer) and interlacing
Singular value decomposition and polar decomposition
Multilinear algebra: tensor products, symmetric and exterior powers
Kronecker products and matrix equations (Sylvester, Lyapunov)

chapters.name: Specialized Algebraic Structures
chapters.summary: A tour of structures that appear in physics and computing: quaternions, octonions, Clifford, Boolean, tensor and exterior algebras.

chapters.name: Order Theory & Lattices
chapters.summary: Partially ordered sets and lattices: Boolean and distributive lattices, Galois connections, fixed-point theorems and their uses in logic and computing.

topics.name: Partially ordered sets, Hasse diagrams, chains and antichains
Lattices as ordered sets and as algebras
Boolean algebras and Stone's representation theorem
Fixed-point theorems (Knaster-Tarski) and domain theory basics
Ordered algebraic structures: ordered groups and fields

chapters.name: Algebraic Coding Theory
chapters.summary: Error-correcting codes built from finite fields and polynomial algebra, such as linear, cyclic, BCH and Reed-Solomon codes.

chapters.name: Commutative Algebra
chapters.summary: Commutative rings and modules (Noetherian rings, localisation, primary decomposition, dimension), the algebraic engine of algebraic geometry and number theory.

topics.name: Dedekind domains and discrete valuation rings

chapters.name: Universal Algebra & General Algebraic Systems
chapters.summary: General algebraic systems studied all at once: varieties of algebras, free algebras, Birkhoff's theorems and equational logic.

topics.name: Algebras, signatures, subalgebras, homomorphisms and congruences
Equational logic and Birkhoff's completeness theorem
Clones, Mal'cev conditions and congruence lattices

chapters.name: Lie Theory
chapters.summary: Continuous symmetry: Lie groups, Lie algebras, root systems and their representations, central to geometry and physics.

topics.name: Matrix Lie groups and examples (SO(n), SU(n), SL(n))
The exponential map and the Lie algebra of a Lie group
Solvable, nilpotent and semisimple Lie algebras
Classification of complex semisimple Lie algebras

chapters.name: Homological Algebra
chapters.summary: Chain complexes, derived functors, Ext and Tor and spectral sequences: the machinery behind modern algebra, topology and geometry.

chapters.name: K-Theory
chapters.summary: Algebraic and topological K-theory, which measure vector bundles and projective modules and connect topology, algebra and index theory.

topics.name: Vector bundles and the Grothendieck group
K-theory of C*-algebras and index theory connections

chapters.name: Elementary Number Theory
chapters.summary: Divisibility, primes, congruences and quadratic reciprocity: the classical theory of the integers and the basis of modern cryptography.

topics.name: Fermat's little theorem and Euler's theorem
Sums of two and four squares

chapters.name: Arithmetic Functions
chapters.summary: Multiplicative functions such as Euler's phi, Moebius and divisor functions, Dirichlet convolution and average orders.

chapters.name: Diophantine Equations
chapters.summary: Finding integer and rational solutions of polynomial equations, from linear and Pell equations to Fermat's Last Theorem.

chapters.name: Cryptographic Number Theory
chapters.summary: The number theory behind public-key cryptography: primality testing, factoring, RSA and discrete logarithms.

chapters.name: Analytic Number Theory
chapters.summary: Uses complex analysis to study primes: the Riemann zeta function, the prime number theorem and Dirichlet L-functions.

topics.name: The Riemann hypothesis and zero-free regions

chapters.name: Algebraic Number Theory
chapters.summary: Number fields and their rings of integers: ideals, class groups, units, valuations and a glimpse of class field theory.

topics.name: Dedekind domains and factorisation of prime ideals

topics.name: p-adic absolute values and Ostrowski's theorem

chapters.name: Transcendental Number Theory

topics.name: Baker's theory of linear forms in logarithms

chapters.name: Elliptic Curves

topics.name: Weierstrass equations and the group law
Elliptic curves over finite fields and Hasse's bound
Elliptic curves over the complex numbers

chapters.name: Modular Forms
chapters.summary: Highly symmetric complex functions (modular and automorphic forms, Hecke operators) at the heart of modern number theory.

topics.name: The modular group and fundamental domain

chapters.name: Additive Combinatorics
chapters.summary: Additive structure in sets of integers: sumsets, Szemeredi's theorem and primes in arithmetic progressions.

chapters.name: Real Analysis
chapters.summary: Rigorous calculus: the real numbers, limits, continuity, differentiation, Riemann integration and uniform convergence, proved from first principles.

topics.name: The real numbers: completeness and the least upper bound property

Differentiation in several variables: inverse and implicit function theorems

Convex functions of one and several variables

Differentiability of functions of several real variables; inverse and implicit function theorems
